## Page contract — read before your first publish

These are the Artifact tool's own rules for the file you publish; the design guidance below builds on them.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Skeleton**: The file is wrapped in a `<!doctype html>…<head>…</head><body>` skeleton at publish time, so write the page content directly — no `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` tags of your own. Its head carries only a charset and viewport meta (with `viewport-fit=cover`) plus a small reset — light `color-scheme`, `:root` padded top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets, zero body margin with a 14px system font, `img{max-width:100%}`, and `[hidden]{display:none!important}` (toggle visibility with `el.hidden`, not `style.display`) — so put your own `<title>` and `<style>` at the top of the file. Keep the `:root` padding. Put `<meta name="claude:viewport-fit-sides" content="cover">` at the top of the file beside your `<title>`: it promises that the side gutter uses the two `max()` paddings given under Responsive, so the tag goes in only together with both paddings, never alone. An edit of an older page that has neither leaves both out, unless the ask redoes the page's layout. With it the page also runs under a system bar at the phone's side, where backgrounds reach that edge while the gutter keeps text and controls clear. Anything fixed to a screen edge stays at `0` and adds that edge's `env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)` to its own padding (one that spans the width takes the side gutter too), a floating or absolutely placed control adds the nearby edges' insets to its offsets, and a sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)`, not `0`, with the band above it painted by a fixed `body::before` (`content: ""; position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto; height: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px); z-index: 10`) in its background, or in the page's where it starts lower.

**Title**: Put a `<title>` at the top of the HTML; only the first 8KB of the file is scanned for it. It is the artifact's name in the browser tab and the gallery, so write a name, not a summary: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific enough to pick this page out among many, the way an app or a document is named. When the user already has a specific name for the thing, use that name for the title rather than coining a new one. Never use a generic category label alone, and never append an explainer after a dash or colon. If you shorten a title that pairs the name with a generic word, keep the name, not the generic word. A multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished; do not shorten it further. The explanation goes in the one-sentence `description` parameter, which becomes the gallery card's subtitle. The `title` parameter fills in only when an HTML file has no `<title>` tag (Markdown pages keep their filename). Keep the title stable across redeploys.

**External resources — CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external scripts load ONLY from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, https://unpkg.com, https://cdn.tailwindcss.com (Tailwind's play-CDN script) and https://code.jquery.com; external stylesheets ONLY from https://fonts.googleapis.com, with the font files they pull from https://fonts.gstatic.com (give every face a real fallback stack). Everything else is blocked, with no visible error: every other host (esm.sh included) and, even on those CDNs, anything but a script — stylesheets, images, media, fetch/XHR/WebSocket, a library's runtime fetches. So inline all other CSS and JS and embed assets as data: URIs. **How to load a library**: `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/<lib>/<exact version>/<file>">` — pick the UMD build, which defines a global (e.g. react/18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js, then react-dom) — placed BEFORE any inline `<script>` that uses it. Pin every library URL to an exact version (`react@18.3.1` on jsDelivr or unpkg, `react/18.3.1/…` on cdnjs, `cdn.tailwindcss.com/3.4.17`), never a bare name, a range or a tag (`react`, `react@18`, `@latest`). Choose a version at least two weeks old. Any version you knew before this conversation is old enough; if you look versions up, skip any published in the last two weeks. The viewer's sandbox also blocks any download the page starts itself — `<a download>` links (data:/blob: hrefs included) and script-driven saves are inert for viewers — so never offer a file through a plain link. Links to other websites (`https://…`) open in a new tab, but email, phone and app links (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`, other custom schemes) are unreliable inside an artifact: for many viewers (for example anyone outside the user's organization, or anyone viewing through a public link) following one, by link or by script, often does not work, and the page cannot tell whether it did. So show the address or number itself as selectable text (a copy button helps), treat such a link as a convenience that may do nothing, and never tell the viewer a message was sent or a call placed because the viewer tapped one. Artifacts render mermaid diagrams natively — markdown via ```mermaid fences, HTML via `<pre class="mermaid">` blocks — no library needed, don't load one. The viewer never shows `alert()`, `confirm()` or `prompt()` dialogs — `confirm()` returns false and `prompt()` returns null immediately — so build any confirmation step into the page itself.

**What the viewer's frame allows**: The page runs in a locked-down frame; what it refuses below, it refuses for every viewer (anonymous, signed-in, embedded, desktop and mobile apps), so build around these limits instead of detecting them. The page cannot open the print dialog — `window.print()` does nothing — so never offer a Print or "Save as PDF" button. Forms work as page UI (inputs, validation, submit events), but a real submission has nowhere to go: handle `submit` in script with `preventDefault()` and never point `action` at another site or a mailto: address. Copy buttons work when `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is called inside the click handler — catch its rejection (older desktop apps and some app views refuse it) and fall back to selecting the text; reading the clipboard never works, though the viewer's own Paste (the `paste` event) does. Camera, microphone, screen capture, location, motion, Web Share and similar device APIs are refused without a prompt — build on one only when this user has a runtime capability for that device (the `artifact-capabilities` skill lists them) and the page declares it; otherwise take photos, audio and data as uploaded files instead (file inputs, drag-and-drop of files and `FileReader` work in browsers). A screen wake lock may be granted while the page is visible: request it and tolerate rejection. Fullscreen and pointer lock work from a click in desktop browsers; treat both as optional (handle the rejection) since phones and some app views lack them. Sound plays only after the viewer interacts (muted autoplay is fine), so start audio from a button. Other sites cannot be embedded — no YouTube, map or form iframes, and no `<object>`/`<embed>`; link out instead: links open outside the artifact, normally in a new tab, while `window.open` works only for some signed-in viewers in the artifact's own organization and returns null for everyone else, so use real `<a href>` links. Web Workers work from your own files or `blob:` URLs; service workers and WebRTC do not. `fetch()` of files published alongside the page works with relative URLs; images from your own files, `data:` or `blob:` URLs draw to canvas and export cleanly. Only a plain `#anchor` (letters, digits, `.` `_` `~` `-`) from the artifact's link reaches `location.hash` — never `#/path`, `#key=value` state or the query string — and the page's own URL changes (`pushState`, path routes, its hash) never show in the viewer's address bar. Only where a page has several views worth bookmarking or sending (tabs, sections, records), name each with a bare token (never `settings`, `sidebar`, `customize`, `upgrade`, `downloads` or anything starting `comment-`, which the viewer keeps), open the one in `location.hash` on load, keep all other state in the page, and give the user each view's link (the artifact's link plus `#token`), because the address bar will not follow them from view to view.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Responsive**: The page must also work at phone width (about 400px), and the page body must never scroll horizontally. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width, written `padding-left: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px))` and `padding-right: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px))` so that it also clears a system bar at the phone's side: set it once on `body` or one outer wrapper (where colored bands span the width, on each band's inner wrapper), and give that element its vertical padding with `padding-block`, never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Use relative units. Let flex and grid rows wrap or stack to one column when narrow, and give any flex or grid child that holds running text, code or a table `min-width: 0`, so long content wraps or scrolls inside it instead of pushing the page wider. Put `max-width: 100%` on images and on any `aspect-ratio` box, and give nothing a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only tables, diagrams and code blocks may be wider, each inside its own `overflow-x: auto` container.

**Theme-aware**: The page renders in the viewer's theme, which has three states: an explicit choice sets `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting sets nothing, so for most viewers only `prefers-color-scheme` tells light from dark. Define every color as a token, in this shape (token names and count are the design's own):
```css
:root { --bg: …; --fg: …; --accent: … }  /* every token, light values */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { --bg: …; --fg: …; --accent: …; color-scheme: dark } }
:root[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: …; --fg: …; --accent: …; color-scheme: dark }  /* same dark values, so the toggle wins both ways */
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg) }
```
Every token gets its first definition on bare `:root`; the two dark blocks only redefine tokens, and their `color-scheme: dark` makes form controls and scrollbars follow. No color has its only definition inside a media or `[data-theme]` block, and no component rule uses a literal color that reads in one theme only. `body` keeps that explicit token background: the viewer paints its own ground behind the page, so a transparent body shows the host's theme instead. A dark-first design mirrors the whole shape, selectors included: dark values and `color-scheme: dark` on bare `:root` (the skeleton pins `light` there), light values and `color-scheme: light` under `(prefers-color-scheme: light)` guarded `:root:not([data-theme="dark"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="light"]`. A design that deliberately commits to a single look may drop the two dark blocks but still sets the background and every color explicitly, plus `color-scheme: dark` on `:root` if that look is dark.

**Icon** (on every first publish): Pass one short generic word as `icon` (e.g. `"chart"`, `"calendar"`, `"recipe"`) for the artifact's browser-tab icon — a plain signifier for what the page is, never a product or brand name, and never an emoji or markup. It stays the **same** for the life of an artifact, so on a redeploy (the same file path this session, or `url`) omit `icon` and the artifact keeps the one it has; pass a different one only when the user asks.

Work the way the design lead at a small, versatile studio would: give each client a visual identity at the level of treatment the task calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Decide the treatment; designing is a given. A doc gets the same craft as a landing page; only the treatment differs. Format is a separate matter: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. A Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title, uses almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished, with real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages don't need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

If unsure: a well-composed page is always acceptable; an over-designed visual identity sometimes isn't.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. Follow the editorial process after them only when that reading calls for it.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Respect what already exists.** Look for an existing design system first: CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, define it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. Distinctive choices come from the subject's own world: its materials, instruments, and vernacular. Whatever the treatment, include at least one detail only this subject would have (its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art) as content rather than ornament; it costs nothing even on a plain page. Use real content throughout and never lorem ipsum.

**Pair typefaces.** Typography determines how the page reads even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the only font host the Artifact CSP allows; link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`). A face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI, or the browser silently uses a fallback. In both cases, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide. Set a type scale and keep to it. Give headings `text-wrap: balance`, give body text comfortable spacing, and give uppercase labels a little letter-spacing.

**Load libraries instead of inlining them.** When the page really needs a library (React, a charting or highlighting package), load its UMD build from cdnjs with one `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">`, pinned to an exact version at least two weeks old and placed before the inline script that uses its global; don't inline the library's source or hand-write a substitute. Only the script loads this way; a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined, and the page contract above lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images, and its data ship with the page. Most pages don't need any library; use one only when it does substantial work for the page.

**Choose neutrals deliberately.** A pure mid-grey looks unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent looks intentional. Pure white and near-black are fine backgrounds when they suit the subject, as long as you chose the neutral deliberately instead of inheriting a default.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states: an explicit choice sets `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting sets *nothing*. Most viewers see the document with no `data-theme` attribute, where only `prefers-color-scheme` distinguishes light from dark. Structure the CSS at the token level for all three. The bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice overrides a dark OS setting; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also overrides in the other direction; wherever the dark palette applies - both dark blocks, or bare `:root` in a dark-first or single-dark design - also set `color-scheme: dark` (the skeleton pins `light` on `:root`), so native form controls and scrollbars follow the palette. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block: a color defined only inside `[data-theme]` never applies when no `data-theme` attribute is set, and the page then shows one theme's text on the other theme's background. Two more rules keep each theme consistent. First, the artifact is composited over a background the viewer paints in *its own* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token; a transparent body shows the host's background with no warning. Second, every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never from a literal that works in only one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it; a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first: don't simply invert it; keep contrast legible and keep the accent working on both backgrounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme: then omit the media query and `[data-theme]` blocks entirely but still set the background and every color explicitly, so the page looks right on either host background; do this by choice, never by omission.

**Use layout for spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap` instead of per-element margins, which collapse or double without warning. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width, written `padding-left: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px))` and `padding-right: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px))` so that it also clears a system bar at the phone's side: set it once on `body` or one outer wrapper (where colored bands span the width, on each band's inner wrapper), whose vertical padding uses `padding-block` and never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (about 400px). Give images and any `aspect-ratio` box `max-width: 100%`, and don't give anything a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only wide tables, code, and diagrams may exceed it; give each `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. The publish skeleton pads `:root` top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets (zero everywhere except a phone app) so the page runs edge to edge while its content stays clear of the system bars; keep that padding. Put `<meta name="claude:viewport-fit-sides" content="cover">` at the top of the file beside your `<title>`: it promises that the side gutter uses those two `max()` paddings, so the tag goes in only together with both paddings, never alone. An edit of an older page that has neither leaves both out, unless the ask redoes the page's layout. With it the page also runs under a system bar at the phone's side. Anything fixed to a screen edge stays at `0` and adds that edge's inset to its own padding (one that spans the width takes the side gutter too); a floating or absolutely placed control adds the nearby edges' insets to its offsets. A sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` and never `0`. So that nothing scrolls into view above it, under the host's controls, paint that band with `body::before { content: ""; position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto; height: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px); z-index: 10; background: ... }`, in the header's own background where the header opens the page and in the page's where the sticky bar starts lower. Size a one-screen app with `height: 100%` on `html` and `body` instead of `100vh`, so it fits inside the `:root` padding. A page that includes its own viewport meta gets the `:root` padding only when that meta declares `viewport-fit=cover`. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Make repeated elements consistent.** For cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, or badges on sibling items, use the same edges, baselines, and inner padding on each, and put any recurring element in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over empty space or sits alone in a row. Make text that can outgrow its track wrap or scroll in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Use card styling selectively.** Border, fill, radius, and shadow each mark an element as a separate object. Apply them by role, to set off the one element that needs it; applying the same radius and shadow to every block flattens the hierarchy. Open with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to scale.** Place marks, ticks, and labels with one scale, and make every label name a value the chart actually reaches. Color chart text from the theme tokens so it is readable in both themes. Keep marks, labels, and edges clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds; in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Make the page complete at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, with no scrolling to trigger it; that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all see. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never left at `opacity: 0` waiting for an observer. Size a hero to its content instead of to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the rest of the page out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state: the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, or a plausibly filled form, clearly marked as examples and never presented as the user's own figures. The first view shows what the tool does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing. When those records live in the `db` capability, keep them out of the page source. Its first frame renders before the store answers, so make that frame a designed empty state that names what will appear and how to add the first entry, then fill it from the store. Seed the store through the `ArtifactData` tool (what type instructions call `write_db`) after the first publish: the user's real data, or marked examples for a tool only the user will use. For a store other people will fill with their own entries, seed only what the user gave you or asked for, never invented people or records.

**Avoid AI-generated design.** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. When the user specifies a visual direction, follow it exactly; their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. When nothing is specified, don't use that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly.** Watch for overlapping elements, cascade collisions, and silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform preserves form values, focus, and scroll position across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, use Canvas or WebGL instead of hand-writing long SVG path data.

**CSS rules.** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificity. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out, e.g. a type-based selector like `.section` and an element-based one like `.cta` both setting padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't undo your spacing unnoticed.

**Writing the copy.** Treat words as design material and never as decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen: name things by what people recognize instead of how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*; they don't manage *webhook config*). Use active voice; a control states exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologies or vagueness. Prefer specific to clever. Write plainly, the way a knowledgeable person would talk. Avoid mannered devices: asides set off by em-dashes, "not X, but Y" framing, colon-then-reveal sentences, scare quotes around invented labels, and stock phrases such as "worth noting" or "honest caveat". Prefer short, direct sentences over compressed or clever phrasing.

**Name the page like a product; don't caption it.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it gives the reader a first impression of the care taken. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject; or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which then is the page's name. When the user already has a specific name for the thing, use that name for the title rather than coining a new one. Stop at the name; a title that adds its own explanation after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it appears beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could apply to any of them fails as a name just as an appended explanation does. When a candidate title combines the name with a generic word (a greeting, a category, a page-type label), keep the name; a trim that drops the identifying part and keeps the generic word produces a title that could apply to any page. This rule removes explanations and doesn't require brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. Put the explanation in the one-sentence publish `description`; the gallery shows it directly under the title.

**Structure is information.** Structural devices (numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels) should encode something true about the content instead of decorating it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but those fit only if the content actually is a sequence, such as a real process or a typed timeline where the order is information the reader needs. Before adding numbered markers or similar devices, check that they actually make sense.

**When the page is a UI (dashboard, tool).** It is scanned and operated instead of read top to bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Put the summary before the detail. Encode state in form as well as in numbers (a pill, a chip, a severity stripe) so that whatever needs attention is visible at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. Interactive elements should look interactive.



## Process

Start from what the viewer should be able to do on the page, in addition to what they will read. If the page should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user. A page that is only read doesn't need that.

Before writing the page, settle a short design plan (a compact token system) and write it into the file itself, as the `:root` block at the top of the page's `<style>`, rather than into your reply:
- **Color**: the palette as 4-6 named color tokens.
- **Type**: font tokens for 2+ roles: a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: the layout concept as a one-line comment above the tokens.

Then build the rest of the page from those tokens, deriving every color and type decision from them. The plan is working material, not part of the answer: unless the user asks about the design, one plain sentence on the direction is the most to say about it, with no hex values or font names.

**Write, check once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once, where this session offers a way: one `ArtifactCheck` preview (or the Artifact tool's own `action: "preview"` where there is no separate `ArtifactCheck` tool), or else one screenshot of the local file; if the session offers none of these, skip the look. The preview renders desktop and phone widths in light and dark and lists overflow, colors that ignore the theme, blocked loads and console errors, including a script that fails to parse, so nothing it covers needs a check of your own. The look is optional: if you take it, make one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look; then publish. For a page that charts real numbers, take the look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. A page whose point is logic (dates, money, scoring, parsing) may get one more check before publishing: one run of a pure function on a sample input, or, where no preview ran, one syntax check of its script; nothing more. A page that declares `capabilities` takes the look rather than skipping it, then one functional pass after the first publish, because the preview cannot run that code: read back once what the page stores or serves (one read of its stored data or one read-only route call; where that read alone would prove nothing, as on an empty store, you may first write one probe document yourself and delete it after the read, passing the `version` the write returned as `if_version`; no other test writes unless the user wants one), tell the user in one line what you exercised and what you could not, and stop. None of this becomes a loop, because the user is waiting for a link: no second screenshot, no scripts that probe the DOM, no re-running a check that passed. Review happens on the live page, and further polish is for the user to request; if the user reports something visibly broken (a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing), fix that, take at most one more look if the session offers a way, and republish once. These checks are for code you wrote into this page, not for content you fill into an Artifact made from an Artifact type (a Slides deck, a Design canvas): there the type's own instructions say whether to check, and if they say nothing, don't.

**Open viewers.** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open: published changes are delivered to them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state preserved where possible. If your page has state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`; `hot` is the viewer's own update hook, not a capability behind `claude.use()`, and is absent outside a viewer, hence the `?.`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance changes here: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated decisions, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part in the plan itself, without narrating the revision to the user. Write the code only after the plan is specific to this subject, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero states the thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (headline, image, live demo, interactive moment). 
- Typography sets the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, avoiding the families you would use on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design instead of a neutral container for the content. 
- Use motion deliberately. Think about whether and where animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. One orchestrated moment is usually more effective than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation adds to the impression that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Put your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent clashes with the background, shift it toward an analogous hue or desaturate it instead of replacing it.

# Cold read of 23 JusPrin screens

I own a Bambu Lab P1S and a Creality Ender-3 V3 KE and signed up a few days ago. I read each screen once, literally, as a busy new user.

## Screen 1 — Home, both printers listed

- "STL · 3MF · STEP · OBJ · AMF · SVG · ZIP" — the file types it accepts.
- "arrow_headband" / "Today" — a project I worked on today.
- "Printing on Bambu Lab P1S · 62%" — this project is printing right now and is 62% done.
- "1 print · 1 printing now" — it has been printed once, and that one is running.
- "Tape dispenser" / "Yesterday" — a project from yesterday.
- "Printed Nov 5 · Bambu Lab P1S · PLA Basic" — it was printed on Nov 5 on the P1S in PLA Basic.
- "2 prints · finished yesterday" — printed twice, and the printing finished yesterday.
- "Tell us how it printed · 25 credits" — if I report how it came out, I get 25 credits.
- "find_my_hollow" / "Nov 3" / "Draft" — a project from Nov 3 that I haven't finished or printed.
- "PRINTERS" — my printers.
- "Bambu Lab P1S" — my P1S.
- "Printing · 62% · 41m left" — it is printing, 62% done, 41 minutes to go.
- "arrow_headband" — the job it is printing.
- "LAN · P1S · 0.4 mm" — connected over my local network, model P1S, 0.4 mm nozzle.
- "PLA, PETG" plus four colour squares (black, white, red, grey) — the materials and colours loaded.

- "1 G-code · never printed" — a print file was made for it but never printed.

**Buttons**
- "Print history" — shows a list of past prints.
- "+ New" — starts an empty project.
- "Open…" — opens a file from my computer.
- "…" on each printer — a menu of printer actions.
- "Launch monitor" — opens something to watch the P1S, maybe a camera or a status window.

**Where I hesitate**
- "PLA, PETG" with four colour squares: two material names, four colours. I can't tell which colour is which material or which slot.
- "Launch monitor": I don't know if this is a camera, a separate app, or a window inside JusPrin.
- "1 G-code · never printed": "G-code" is a word I half know. "Never printed" makes me wonder why the file exists and whether something failed.
- "192.168.1.42 isn't answering." gives no hint what to check: is the printer off, did its address change, is it on another network?
- "Reconnect" doesn't say whether it will ask me for anything or just retry.
- "find_my_hollow … Draft": "Draft" suggests I never sliced it. (Later I see it was exported, which contradicts this.)
- "Printed Nov 5" next to "Yesterday" and "finished yesterday": three ways of saying a date on one card; I had to check they agree.
- "2 prints · finished yesterday": did both prints finish, or only the last one?

- "✓ Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle · Already in JusPrin".
- "✓ Creality Ender-3 V3 KE 0.4 nozzle · Already in JusPrin".
- "☑ Voron 2.4 350 0.4 nozzle" — ticked, will be imported.
- "~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer" — where it looked.

**Buttons**
- "Choose another folder…" — look somewhere else.
- "Cancel" — don't import.
- "Import 1 printer" — import the Voron.

**Where I hesitate**
- The window has no title. I don't know which button got me here.
- I don't own a Voron. Why is it in OrcaSlicer, and why is it pre-ticked?
- "printer connections": addresses and passwords? Would the Voron then appear in my Home printers list as a printer I own?
- "Already in JusPrin": if I changed the P1S settings in OrcaSlicer, are those changes ignored?
- I still don't know what OrcaSlicer is in relation to JusPrin.

---

## Screen 20 — Import result (no title)

**Text**
- "It is in the printer menu. The printer this project uses didn't change."
- "✓ Voron 2.4 350 0.4 nozzle · Imported".
- "⚠ Sunlu Silk PLA · It inherits from a filament this app does not have."
- "✓ 0.24mm Draft @Voron · Imported".
- "2 of 3 filaments imported: Polymaker PolyTerra PLA @Voron, eSUN PETG (OrcaSlicer)."

**Buttons**
- "Done" — close.

**Where I hesitate**
- "It is in the printer menu.": what is "It"? Which menu? I haven't seen a printer menu on Home.
- "The printer this project uses didn't change.": which project? I'm in settings.
- "It inherits from a filament this app does not have.": jargon. Was Sunlu Silk PLA imported or not? What do I do now?
- The list mixes a printer, a filament and a settings preset ("0.24mm Draft @Voron") with no labels saying which is which.
- The two filaments that did import are only in the footnote, not in the list. The one that failed is in the list.
- "eSUN PETG (OrcaSlicer)": why does that one carry "(OrcaSlicer)" on its name?
- "this app" here, "JusPrin" elsewhere.
- Still no title.

---

## Screen 21 — Import: nothing to import

**Text**
- "Every printer in this OrcaSlicer folder is already in JusPrin, so there is nothing to import."
- The P1S and Ender listed as "Already in JusPrin".
- "~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer".

**Buttons**
- "Choose another folder…", "Close".

**Where I hesitate**
- Mostly clear. Filaments aren't mentioned: if I added new filaments in OrcaSlicer, are they skipped?
- No title.

---

## Screen 22 — Import: OrcaSlicer folder not found

**Text**
- "JusPrin didn't find OrcaSlicer's folder on this computer. If OrcaSlicer keeps its settings somewhere else, choose that folder."
- "Looked in" — followed by nothing.

**Buttons**
- "Cancel", "Choose the folder…".

**Where I hesitate**
- "Looked in" with no path after it looks broken. Where did it look?
- I have no idea where OrcaSlicer keeps its settings, so "choose that folder" is no help.
- If I don't use OrcaSlicer, why am I on this screen?

---

## Screen 23 — Import: no printers in the folder

**Text**
- "JusPrin found no OrcaSlicer printers in this folder. If OrcaSlicer keeps its settings somewhere else, choose that folder."
- "Looked in ~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer".

**Buttons**
- "Cancel", "Choose the folder…".

**Where I hesitate**
- The folder exists but has no printers. Did I pick the wrong folder or is OrcaSlicer empty?
- "~/Library" is hidden on a Mac; I wouldn't know how to browse to another such folder.

---

## The 10 problems that would bother me most

1. **Screen 2**: the P1S card says "Needs attention · at 71%" and "Filament ran out. Load new filament, then resume the print.", but the project card still says "Printing on Bambu Lab P1S · 62%" and both say "1 printing now". There is no Resume button, only "Launch monitor".
2. **Screens 6 and 7**: my P1S prints show "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C" and "0.20mm Strength @BBL X1C". X1C isn't my printer, and I'd worry the wrong settings were used.
3. **Screens 6, 7 and 1**: one Tape dispenser print shows only "Started · Bambu Lab P1S 14:12 →" with no ending, but Home says "2 prints · finished yesterday". The same entry says "File no longer kept · slice again to print it", with no slice button and no reason given.
4. **Screens 1, 2 and 9**: the Ender is "1 G-code · never printed" and "Ready · last print cancelled" on Home, and history shows "1 G-code · 0 prints". Its project "find_my_hollow" is called "Draft" even though history shows "✓ Exported find_my_hollow.gcode … matches, checked just now".
5. **Screen 20**: "It is in the printer menu. The printer this project uses didn't change." doesn't say what "It", which menu or which project. "Sunlu Silk PLA · It inherits from a filament this app does not have." gives no next step and doesn't say whether it was imported.
6. **Screen 22**: "Looked in" is followed by nothing, which looks broken. "choose that folder" assumes I know where OrcaSlicer keeps its settings.
7. **Screens 10 and 19**: "OrcaSlicer preferences… ↗ Every OrcaSlicer setting, as OrcaSlicer shows it." and "JusPrin found 1 printer in OrcaSlicer…". Nothing tells me what OrcaSlicer is or whether I need it. The import also pre-ticks a "Voron 2.4 350 0.4 nozzle" I don't own, under a dialog with no title.
8. **Screen 10**: "Only messages you send cost credits." never says how many credits a message costs, and "Tier Expert" is never explained. "Expiring credits are used first." hints at another kind of credit I can't see, and "Get more credits" shows no price.
9. **Screen 8**: "A photo of the printed object and a few sentences earn 25 credits." doesn't say who sees my photo or what 25 credits are worth. It doesn't say which fields unlock "Send report" either, and "0 of 200 characters" is too short for "a few sentences".
10. **Screen 11**: ""Found" means JusPrin found the app or its settings file here… You can connect one that wasn't found." points to a list of apps that isn't on the screen, so there's nothing to connect. "you don't need to know what MCP is" brings up jargon I'd never heard of.

######## bc
## The problems that would bother me most

1. **b / screen-04**: "1 filament imported: Bambu PLA Basic @BBL P1S." The screen before (b / screen-03) promised "Also brings 14 filaments." 13 profiles vanished with no reason, no list and no retry.
2. **c / screen-03**: "Sign up and get 500 free credits" / "Sign in for 500 credits", shown to a returning JusPrin v1 user. I'd already have an account, and nothing says whether it, or what I paid for in v1, carries over.
3. **b / screen-05**: The "AGENT" section shows only "500 credits left" and "Sign-up credits 500 of 500 left". There's no visible place to talk to the AI, which was the whole reason I signed up.
4. **b / screen-01**: "Use your own AI account … Free". It isn't free, because my provider bills me (c / screen-02 says "Billed by your provider, not JusPrin").
5. **b / screen-03**: "Choose my printer instead". I can't tell if it skips the import or picks which imported printer is active.
6. **b / screen-02**: After signing up, the page still says "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice." and still offers "Just slice for now". I'd fear clicking it throws away my sign-up.
7. **c / screen-02**: "JusPrin writes the connection settings; you don't need to know what MCP is." It names a term just to dismiss it, and doesn't say which files or apps it changes.
8. **b / screen-05**: "3 prints · 1 printing now", "1 G-code · never printed", "Last connected 1 day ago". That's history in an app I installed minutes ago, with no hint where it came from.
9. **c / screen-01** and **c / screen-02**: "Sign up and get 500 free credits" above a button reading "Sign in for 500 credits". As someone without an account, I don't know if "Sign in" is the right button.
10. **b / screen-01**: "Sign up and get 500 free credits … Good for your first month … After that, 50 free credits a month." I don't know what a credit is beyond "about 100 messages", whether leftovers expire, or what it costs after that. And "Photo credits" on the same screen muddles the word further.
######## e1
## The 12 problems that would bother me most

1. **screen-004**: "Resolve pending actions before deleting this chat." Nothing on screen looks pending, so I can't do what it asks.
2. **screen-012**: "Wait for the current action to finish before deleting." What action? Nothing shows it or how long it takes, and it's worded differently from screen-004 for what seems the same block.
3. **screen-002**: "The native host did not answer the hello handshake." Developer jargon, and when "Retry" fails there's no next step.
4. **screen-005**: summary "Stop the corners lifting / Wide brim and a slow first layer for adhesion" under my request "Make it strong, but keep the screw holes accurate". The summary contradicts the conversation and the title "Strong print".
5. **screen-026**: "The Agent is not available". No reason (offline? signed out? out of credits?) and no way to fix it.
6. **screen-016**: "Connect an Agent to continue this conversation". On a list of three chats, which conversation? And what is "an Agent" I connect: an account, a key, a cost?
7. **screen-045**: after "Slice it" nothing shows that slicing started or finished. Also, from screen-044 ("Shall I slice it now?") I can't tell whether slicing also sends the file to the printer.
8. **screen-021**: "Could not be attached". No reason and no retry, and I don't know whether Send will go without it.
9. **screen-011**: "Your model and print history will stay." Does "model" mean my 3D model or the AI model? And it says nothing about whether the 7 settings this chat changed stay or are undone.
10. **screen-031**: "Thinking: Medium" and the model names ("Claude Opus 5.5", and in screen-037 "Claude Sonnet 5.5" listed twice, once under "OPENROUTER"). No hint about what changes, cost or speed, or which duplicate to pick.
11. **screen-046**: "Open filament settings" in purple bold at the top of an empty chat. I can't tell whether it's a title or a button. In screen-047 the same header sits over a conversation about part strength.
12. **screen-004**: "Generic ABS +2 · 7 settings changed". What is "+2", who changed the 7 settings, and are they applied? Screen-042 shows "7 settings changed" in a chat with no messages yet.

Close runners-up:
- **screen-015**: "Configure Agent" greyed out with no reason.
- **screen-030** and **screen-039**: overlapping or empty menus ("Search models" covering "High", and a blank white box).
- **screen-019**: the "bracket-photo.png" thumbnail is a plain purple square, not the photo.
######## e2
## The 12 problems that would bother me most

1. **075**: "Project restoration needs recovery. This chat cannot run project actions." There's no button or instruction for the recovery, and "Agent working" shows at the same time. I don't know whether my project is safe or what to do.
2. **072**: "This chat has no recoverable project checkpoint. Its saved state is missing or corrupt." "Corrupt" makes me fear my project file is damaged. Nothing says what was lost or what to do.
3. **070**: "There have been project updates since this chat. Restore its saved project version to continue." Nothing here says that restoring replaces my current work. "Return to active chat" and "Ask current chat about this" don't say which chat they mean.
4. **074**: "Restore "Quick print" from 2026-10-03T12:00:00Z? … with the matching intent and plan." The raw timestamp doesn't match "Saved Oct 3, 05:00" on the card. "intent and plan" is jargon, and "remain in history" doesn't say where to find it.
5. **086**: "This conversation will be closed. You can't continue it at a later point." I likely just pressed Back during printer setup. I can't tell whether my printer is added or the setup is lost.
6. **052 / 055**: "Use **four walls" followed by "Stopped". The raw asterisks look broken, the sentence is cut off, and I don't know who stopped it or whether four walls were applied.
7. **065**: "Layer height 0.20 → 0.20 mm" is listed as one of "6 settings" under "Laid flat". It isn't a change, none of the rows is about laying flat, and nothing says whether the changes are applied or only proposed.
8. **087**: "Sign up and get 500 free credits", but the button says "Sign in for 500 credits". "50 free credits a month" works out to about 10 messages, and nothing says what happens when they run out.
9. **094**: "Working, but only until JusPrin restarts". This sits under a heading that says "Stored on this computer only", with no reason and no fix. The chat will just stop working after a restart.
10. **062**: "Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · Oct 1". "a71f 8c04" is meaningless to me, and the arrow doesn't say whether it was sent, printed, or failed.
11. **060**: "JusPrin said more than fits here." There's no way to see the rest. It also makes me unsure whether these file notes came from the file or from the app.
12. **080 / 084**: "Found on your network" lists "Workshop M4 · Offline" and "DEMO-A1-2048". I can't tell whether the rows are clickable, how an offline printer was found, or whether "DEMO" means it isn't my real printer.

input.content:
JusPrin wording sweep, 6 November 2026

This lists the places on JusPrin's own screens where a first-time user would misread the text or get stuck. Each one has a proposed rewording. Nothing has been changed in the code, and nothing has been put on the JusPrin v2 canvas. Every rewording below is a proposal waiting for Kenneth's pick.

Text and code were checked on the jusprin-newui-integration branch. Each problem shows the screen, the exact text, what a person would think, the proposal, where the code shows the proposal is true, and who caught it.

Cold reader caught it A fresh agent who only saw the screenshots flagged this. Only my reading The cold reader passed over it; I found it reading the screen against the code.
HomePrint historyProject chatPrinter chat PreferencesImport from OrcaSlicerWelcome back Main windowFirst launchCanvas coverage How this was checkedDecision needed

Home

Sam has a P1S printing, a Tape dispenser printed yesterday, and a project whose G-code was exported for an Ender.

A project whose G-code was exported is called a draft

On screen
find_my_hollow … Draft, while print history shows ✓ Exported find_my_hollow.gcode.
What they think
"Draft" means the project was never sliced or finished. The person exported it and may have printed it from a card, so the card contradicts the history page.
Proposal
When the latest G-code was exported and not sent: G-code exported Nov 3 for Ender-3 V3 KE. Keep "Draft" only for projects with no G-code.
Code
Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp ledger_text has three cases: "Printed", "Sent", and "Draft" for everything else. Export is not a case.
Caught by
Cold reader caught it

The report invitation joins an action and a reward with a dot

On screen
Tell us how it printed · 25 credits (also a button on each print-history entry).
What they think
The dot reads as a price: telling costs 25 credits. A person who does read it as a reward doesn't know what a credit buys.
Proposal
Report how it printed and get 25 credits
Code
HomeUI/src/history.ts REPORT_OFFER. The reward is REPORT_CREDITS, paid for a sent report, so "get" is true.
Caught by
Cold reader caught it (partly: it asked what a credit is worth)

"Never printed" says something the app can't know

On screen
1 G-code · never printed on the Ender card, and Exported once · never printed on project cards and in the project pane.
What they think
The print failed or the file is broken. In fact, someone who exported G-code to a card and printed it from the printer's screen is told they never printed.
Proposal
G-code exported once. JusPrin hasn't seen it printed.
Code
HomeUI/src/history.ts:61 and :97, Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:316. These lines count only prints the app sent or watched. An export is recorded but the print from the card is not.
Caught by
Cold reader caught it (it asked why the file exists if it never printed)

"Printer settings…" opens a chat, not settings

On screen
Printer settings…. In the main window's filament menu, Filament settings… does the same.
What they think
A settings window will open. A chat panel opens instead, and Orca's settings window is one step further inside it.

Canvas coverage

I listed the screens and states from the code and checked them against the JusPrin v2 canvas boards (240 files). Most screens have boards: the Agent page, setup card, printer chat, Preferences, Home, print history, check print, calibration, import, the plates pane and first launch. These screens have no board I could find:

  • The print issue pill and its bubble on the 3D view, including "Checking…" and "Ignored".
  • The banner and View-menu row for returning from the classic view.
  • The tool strip over the 3D view.
  • The welcome-back window, apart from its credits block on the credits boards.
  • The panel's start-up failure and its Diagnostics, apart from one agent board.

How this was checked

  • Web pages (Agent page, Preferences, Home, print history, import, first launch, welcome back) were built from jusprin-newui-integration and driven in Chrome through a fake host that sends the app's real messages for one person, Sam, with two printers and three projects. The chat states come from the page's own state gallery.
  • Native panes were drawn to bitmaps by the shell test harness built from jusprin-newui at b0a2fe3b08, and every string was then checked on the integration branch. Whole-window captures came out black because the screen was locked, so the native screens are close-ups from the harness's test project, not a walk through Sam's day.
  • Cold readers: five fresh agents each got only screenshots with neutral file names and one line of context. Several false alarms came from my own test data disagreeing between screens (for example a printer that was printing on one card and stopped on another); those are left out.
  • My own reading checked each screen against the five wording patterns: facts joined by a dot, metaphors, mechanism instead of action, internal labels, and hints instead of consequences. I then checked each claim and proposal against the code. Where a proposal depends on something I couldn't confirm, the item says "unverified".
  • Stock OrcaSlicer screens and text are out of scope. Fork ownership was checked with git blame and git branch -r --contains against upstream/*.

Decision needed

Decision needed: On Home, "Printer settings…" in a printer's menu opens a chat about that printer, and "Filament settings…" in the main window's filament menu does the same. Orca's settings window is one step inside each chat. This is yours because it decides whether settings go through the agent by default. One option is to keep the chat and rename both items to "Ask about this printer's settings…" and "Ask about this filament's settings…", which is a two-string change. The other is to open Orca's settings window directly and offer the chat from inside it, which needs new wiring in two places. I'd rename. Should the menu items open the chat under a new name, or open the settings window?

Decision needed: Print history entries, the report form and the chat's G-code marker show the first eight characters of the G-code's hash, such as "7c1e 9a40". Every cold reader who saw it found it meaningless. This is yours because the hash was put there on purpose, likely so two files with the same name can be told apart. One option is to remove it from view and keep it in a tooltip, which costs nothing because entries already show their time. The other is to keep it but label it ("file 7c1e 9a40"), which still means nothing to most people. I'd remove it from view. Should the hash come off the screen?

Decision needed: When JusPrin didn't see a print finish, history shows "Started · Bambu Lab P1S 14:12 →" with an empty end, and a G-code with no print it saw reads "never printed". Your 2026-10-27 decision is that nothing says a print failed. Separately, PrinterCard.tsx:42 can still show "last print failed", which goes against that decision. This is yours because it is about what the app claims to know. One option is to say what the app saw: "JusPrin didn't see it finish" and "JusPrin hasn't seen it printed". The other is to keep the short words, which people read as stuck or broken. I'd use the "JusPrin didn't see" wording and remove "last print failed". Should history say what JusPrin saw rather than what happened?

Decision needed: In the printer chat, the "Send report" button after a failed connection only saves the report on this computer, because sending isn't built. This is yours because it decides whether a feature that doesn't exist yet is shown. One option is to hide the button until sending exists, which costs the saved reports you might want later. Another is to rename it "Save report" and say where it went, which keeps the data but gives the person nothing. A third is to build sending. I'd hide it until sending exists. Should the button be hidden, renamed, or built out?

Decision needed: The agent has several names: "the Agent" with a capital A in the chat and Preferences, "AI agent" on the welcome page, "Ask AI" on the 3D view, "the assistant" in the issue chat, and "allowance" for credits in one error. This is yours because it is the product's name for its main feature. One option is "the agent", lowercase, everywhere a person reads, which is a text sweep across both web pages and the native panes. The other is to keep "AI" on buttons for recognition and "the agent" in sentences. I'd use "the agent" everywhere, with buttons reading "Ask the agent". Should the agent have one name everywhere?

Decision needed: The welcome-back window offers a JusPrin v1 user the sign-up credits but doesn't say their v1 account doesn't carry over. On 2026-11-04 you said v1 users will be told to sign up again and their subscriptions moved by hand. This is yours because it is a promise to paying customers. One option is to add only "Your JusPrin v1 account doesn't carry over to this version. Sign up again to get 500 free credits." The other is to also add "If you had a v1 subscription, we'll move it to your new account.", which commits support to doing that for everyone who reads it. I'd add both if the manual move is firm. Should the window promise to move v1 subscriptions?

Where a first-time user gets stuck

I walked JusPrin’s first launch on every path I could reach and found 23 places a newcomer is likely to misread or stall. Each orange number marks the spot on the screenshot; the same number below says what is on screen, why it confuses, and a proposed fix.

The proposals are mine and nothing is decided. The app freeze after Import is left out because another session is fixing it.

The welcome screen

  1. 1

    The only buttons are “Continue with Google” and “Continue with email”. The line under them says “New or existing account, same door.”

    A new person looks for “Sign up” or “Create account” and finds neither, so they wonder whether they need an account from somewhere else first. You flagged this one.

    ProposalLead with signing up: the email button reads “Sign up free”, with a small “Already have an account? Sign in” link under it. Both still send the same email code; only the words change.

  2. 2

    Above the three boxes: “Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent.”

    The boxes are three ways to pay for or connect the agent, not ways of thinking. The person doesn’t know yet what the agent is, what Preferences is, or why they must choose now.

    ProposalSay what the choice is: “Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice.”

  3. 3

    “An Expert message is 5 credits.”

    “Expert” appears nowhere else on the screen, so the person can’t tell what 500 credits buys.

    ProposalSay it in things the person does, for example “500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent”. The number needs checking against real costs.

  4. 4

    “Your own API key — Free” and “Claude Code or Claude Desktop — Free · MCP server”.

    “API key” and “MCP server” are developer words. “Free” beside them makes the 500-credit offer look like the expensive choice, and an API key isn’t free: the person pays the AI company directly.

    ProposalFold both into one quieter link, “Use your own AI account instead”, and explain the two options on the screen it opens.

Signing in with email

  1. 5

    The card asks “How do you want to sign in?” and offers a Password box with “Forgot password”. The line that tells a new person what to do, “New here? The code makes your account.”, is the smallest text on the card.

    A new person has no password. A password box suggests they should already have one.

    ProposalShow only “Email me a 6-digit code” at first, with a small “Use a password instead” link for people who set one.

Typing the emailed code

  1. 6

    “The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device.”

    It reads like a riddle. It means the app signs you in as soon as you type the last digit, and you can open the email on your phone.

    Proposal“Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone.”

  2. 7

    “Use the browser instead”.

    Nothing says what happens in the browser. It means “sign in with Google instead”.

    Proposal“Sign in with Google instead”.

Waiting for Google

  1. 8

    “Finish signing in in your browser.”

    The doubled “in” reads as a typo.

    Proposal“Finish in your browser.”

The printer step, signed in

  1. 9

    “Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits”. Your screenshot showed the same line on the OrcaSlicer import screen.

    The person just got 500 credits, and the line doesn’t say so. “500 credits” after a dot reads like a balance they had before. You flagged this one.

    Proposal“You got 500 free credits for signing up.” with the email address on a smaller line under it.

  2. 10

    “OrcaSlicer printers in another folder? Choose the folder…”

    It shows to everyone the app found no OrcaSlicer folder for, which includes everyone who has never used OrcaSlicer.

    ProposalRemove it here. The File › Import › “Import from OrcaSlicer…” menu item covers this later, once it is built.

  3. 11

    “Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours.” The code shows that Skip installs OrcaSlicer’s “Generic Klipper Printer”: a 250 × 250 mm bed and Klipper G-code.

  1. 13

  2. 14

    The count is easy to miss and the path means nothing to most people.

  1. 17

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
description: 2026-11-06 Kenneth: JusPrin work commits to jusprin-newui-integration, never jusprin-newui; tsd-enterprise server code commits straight to master

From 2026-11-06, commit JusPrin app work to the local branch `jusprin-newui-integration`, never to `jusprin-newui`.
Server code in tsd-enterprise goes straight to `master`. Kenneth's words, relayed by the session that started
the account-box work: "tell the subsessions to commit server code directly to master branch. for the JusPrin
repo, create a integration branch, and tell these subsessions to move their commits to the new integration branch."

**Why:** the integration branch collects work so it can be merged into `jusprin-newui` cleanly later.

**How to apply:** `jusprin-newui` is checked out in the shared main checkout, so commit to the integration branch
without switching branches there (a worktree on that branch, or `git branch -f` fast-forwards). Push nothing
unless asked. Supersedes the landing question in [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]].
description: "2026-11-06: Kenneth removed the AGENTS.md rule 'land feature branches on jusprin-newui with --no-ff, never squash' (removal commit 96c7bda756). No standing rule; ask how to land."

On 2026-11-05 Kenneth asked whether to squash for a clean log; I recommended `git merge --no-ff` and he said "Okay, go with what you suggested." I wrote that into AGENTS.md as "Landing a branch on jusprin-newui" (a2d5550058), in my own words, and later called it "the project rules" to him.

On 2026-11-06 he asked where the rule said that, then asked to remove it. Removed in 96c7bda756 on claude/first-run-fixes (reaches jusprin-newui only when that branch lands).

**Why:** the rule text was mine, not his; he had agreed to one recommendation, not to a standing rule. See [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].

**How to apply:** don't cite --no-ff-only as a project rule. When landing a branch, ask Kenneth how he wants it landed (merge or squash) unless he has said so for that branch.
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

You are working in the git worktree /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/wording-sweep-fixes (branch claude/wording-sweep-fixes). It is JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer. Read AGENTS.md at the worktree root first (wording rules, "the app" rule for model-facing text). Do NOT commit, stash, reset, or switch branches. Other uncommitted edits in this worktree are mine (print history, Home printer menu, filament menu, PrinterConversation issue tool): leave them alone, never revert them.

## Task
The product owner decided on 2026-11-06: "Let's consolidate on "AI" everywhere". The AI chat feature is currently called several names in text a person reads: "the Agent", "Agent panel", "the agent", "an agent", "the assistant". Replace every such name in **text a person reads** with "AI", making only the grammar changes the swap needs. Examples of the intended result:
- "Set up the agent" / "Set up the agent…" → "Set up AI" / "Set up AI…"
- "The assistant is replying..." → "AI is replying…"
- "The Agent is not available" → "AI is not available"
- Preferences section title "Agent" → "AI" (the visible title and aria-label; keep the internal section id 'agent' unchanged)
- "Hide the Agent panel" → "Hide the AI panel"; "Message the Agent" → "Message AI"
- "Ask the agent" → "Ask AI"; "messages to the agent" → "messages to AI"
- "Connect an Agent to continue this conversation" → "Set up AI to continue this conversation"
- "Agent allowance" → "AI allowance" (only the name; do not reword further)
Do not rewrite sentences beyond the name swap and the grammar it forces. Other rewordings that were proposed but not approved must NOT be applied (for example do not change the welcome headline, do not reword error messages beyond the name).

## Where to look
- Web pages: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src, HomeUI/src, WebShared/ (TypeScript/TSX: JSX text, aria-labels, titles, string literals shown on screen).
- Native fork code under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/: `_L("…")`, `_u8L("…")` strings and other strings shown to the person, e.g. Shell/StatusRow.cpp, Shell/ShellController.cpp (calibration confirm text, "Set up the agent…"), Agent/AgentWebView.cpp (error panel), PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.cpp, Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp error messages (check whether they are shown to the person; they are AgentError messages shown on a failed reply).
- Starting grep: `grep -rnP "(?<![-_.\w'/])(Agent|agent|assistant|Assistant)(?![-_\w:(])" --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts' --include='*.cpp'` under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin, then judge each hit.

## Leave unchanged
- Text the model reads: AgentUI/src/*Instructions.ts, AgentUI/src/skills/**, tool names/descriptions in Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp, notes posted to the model (post_note), tool results, prompt text. Those call the product "the app" and are guarded by AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts. If a string is BOTH shown to the person and sent to the model, say so in your report and leave it.
- Identifiers, CSS classes, data-testid, protocol values ('agent', 'assistant' roles, actor: 'agent'), section ids, file names, log lines, exceptions, code comments.
- OrcaSlicer-owned files (anything outside src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/ and tests/): do not touch.
- The welcome/onboarding page (HomeUI Onboarding.tsx, AgentUI welcome): apply only the bare name swap, no other rewording.

## Tests
Update tests that pin the old strings: vitest tests in AgentUI and HomeUI, and native tests under tests/jusprin/ and tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp (string matches, ui_name("…") lookups). Run the web tests:
`export PATH=/Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin:$PATH; cd <worktree>/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npx vitest run` and the same in HomeUI. Also `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in each. Both must pass. Do NOT run a native build; I will build afterwards. AgentUI also has visual cases (src/visual/*.visual-cases.tsx) with expected strings; update those that pin old text.

## Report back (under 400 words)
1. A list of every string changed: old → new, with file:line.
2. Strings you found but left, and why (model-facing, both, upstream-owned, unsure).
3. Test results (counts) for AgentUI and HomeUI vitest and tsc.

--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

- **Settings menus:** in Home's printer menu, the main window's printer menu and the filament menu, "Printer settings…" and "Filament settings…" now open Orca's settings window. A new "Ask AI about printer settings…" or "Ask AI about filament settings…" item under each one opens the chat.
- **GitHub issue tool:** Klipper and OctoPrint connection chats now offer it too.

I'll carry on when the helper agent and the build report back.
