content.text:
I built the agreed wording-sweep fixes and committed them as a5c7620776 on a new branch, `claude/wording-sweep-fixes`, cut from `jusprin-newui-integration`. Nothing is pushed or merged yet.

**What changed**
- **"AI" is the one name.** People now read "AI" in:
  - the panel and its error screens;
  - Preferences › AI;
  - the Home card ("Set up AI");
  - the print-issue bubble ("Set up AI…", "AI is replying…");
  - the calibration prompt;
  - the error messages on a failed reply.
  
  Text the model reads still calls the product "the app".
- **Settings menus open the settings window.** In Home's printer menu, the main window's printer menu and the filament menu, "Printer settings…" and "Filament settings…" now open OrcaSlicer's settings window. A new "Ask AI about printer settings…" or "Ask AI about filament settings…" row under each one opens the chat. The main window's printer menu wasn't in the report, but it had the same item behaving the same way, so I changed it too.
- **G-code hashes are gone** from the print history, its search, the report form and the chat's G-code marker.
- **No outcome words.** A Home printer card says only "last print finished"; a failed or cancelled print shows nothing. In the print history, a print that nobody saw end no longer gets a row; its "Sent to …" row still says whether it was started.
- **"never printed" now reads "…, never sent to a printer"**, on Home and in the project pane.
- **The prefilled GitHub issue is offered in Klipper and OctoPrint connection chats too.** The issue's footer names the program, Moonraker or OctoPrint.

**Tests**
- Agent page tests: 692 of 692 pass. Home page tests: 157 of 157 pass.
- Native tests: 168 of 168 JusPrin cases and 556 of 556 agent cases pass. Five agent tests had pinned the old rule that print-host chats get no GitHub tool; I updated them to the new rule.
- The shell harness, which drives the real app, passed in its default, printer-menu and print-issues runs. Those runs include new checks that both settings rows open the window and keep the printer selected.
- The printer-setup and home-live runs each failed. The two failing checks I identified, one in each run, also failed in an earlier session's run on the base code, so I'm treating them as already broken there. The Home page has no "Online" text to find.
- Not checked in the running app: Home's "Printer settings…" opening the settings window. It uses the same call as the chat's "open settings" button, which the harness does check.

**Left out**
- The proposals you haven't approved, including the "Share how it printed and get 25 credits" wording, the new welcome headline, and the fuller rewordings such as "Sign in or add a key to chat with AI".
- The "Send report" card after a failed connection still only saves the report on this computer. Pointing it at the GitHub issue is still my proposal, not something you've agreed.
- I kept "Finished" on prints JusPrin watched and on the Home card. That is my reading of your "no outcome words" rule, and you haven't confirmed it.
Squash it

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about

Each time you run this, it empties the staging data folder, so the app starts as a new install and shows the onboarding flow (welcome, then printers, then Home):

```bash
D="$HOME/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2-stg"; rm -rf "$D" && mkdir -p "$D" && printf '{"jusprin_server":{"base_url":"https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io"}}\n' > "$D/JusPrin2.conf" && "/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/wording-sweep-fixes/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer" --datadir "$D"
```

- **Why it shows onboarding:** the app shows the flow when its config has no onboarding status saved, and no saved projects exist. An empty folder has neither.
- **It won't bring in your v1 data.** The app doesn't import from your v1 JusPrin folder when it's given its own data folder. So you see the new-user flow, not the welcome-back window.
- **It talks to staging.** The one setting it writes makes sign-in go to `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io`. I haven't checked that sign-in works.
- **To keep what you set up,** drop everything before `"/Users/…/OrcaSlicer"` and run just the app with `--datadir "$HOME/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2-stg"`. The folder is then left as it is, and onboarding won't show again once you've finished it.

`jusprin-newui-integration` has six commits that `jusprin-newui` doesn't have, and `jusprin-newui` hasn't moved since the integration branch was cut from it. Five of them are separate changes and read cleanly on their own. One pair is worth squashing.

| Commit | What it is | Squash? |
|---|---|---|
| 8acb12318c | Design guidelines doc (3 files, docs only) | Keep on its own |
| 3e5034e194 | Preferences › Account shows the box the server fills | Keep on its own |
| 6f459dc81e | First launch matches the first-run boards: sign-up card, own-account card, skip note, import result | **Squash with cf2fae27f8** |
| e6ef45798a | OrcaSlicer's cloud login kept in its encrypted file, not the keychain (one file) | Keep on its own |
| cf2fae27f8 | First launch and File › Import: no Retry on the import result | **Squash into 6f459dc81e** |
| a5c7620776 | Wording sweep: "AI", settings menus, no hashes, no outcome words | Keep on its own |

**Why that pair:** both change the same OrcaSlicer import-result screen, in the same files (`OrcaImporter.cpp`, `Onboarding.tsx` and their tests). They were made the same day. 6f459dc81e's message says "Retry still shows only for an unreadable file or a preset that failed to load". The next commit, cf2fae27f8, removes that Retry button. Read one after the other, the log describes a button that no longer exists. As one commit, it would describe the first launch as it now is.

**Why not the others:** the wording sweep also changes a line the first-launch commit added ("messages to the agent" becomes "messages to AI"). That rename comes from a separate decision, so it reads better on its own.

**Decision needed:** should I squash the two first-launch commits before you merge?
- **What it costs:** `origin/jusprin-newui-integration` is pushed at cf2fae27f8, so squashing needs a force-push of that branch. All six commits get new ids. The only other branches holding these commits are the finished work branches `claude/first-run-board-fixes` and `claude/wording-sweep-fixes`, so nothing still in progress is affected.
- **Keeping all six** needs no force-push. The cost is a log where one commit describes a Retry button that the next commit removes.
- **My pick:** squash, and write one combined message.

"""Model aliases for the JusPrin v2 gateway.

The client only ever sees an alias such as "slicer-1". What an alias means
upstream lives in the JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES setting, a JSON env var; nothing
about an upstream model is in code. Upstream keys stay in env vars that the
config names, never in the JSON itself.

Shape (every key shown is required unless marked optional; unknown keys are an
error so a typo fails at startup instead of silently changing routing):

    {
      "aliases": [                         # display order of the models endpoint
        {
          "id": "slicer-1",                # the only model id the client sees
          "label": "Slicer 1",
          "tier": "expert",                # "basic" or "expert"; basic is "Standard" to people
          "credits": 5,                    # what a message costs; efforts cost the same
          "efforts": ["fast", "thorough"], # display order; may be empty
          "default_effort": "fast",        # one of efforts, or null when efforts is empty
          "backends": {                    # keyed by wire format, at least one of:
            "anthropic": {                 #   POST <base_url>/messages, Anthropic Messages API
              "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"},  # must cover every effort
              "headers": {"anthropic-version": "2023-06-01"},     # optional, extra request headers
              "images": true                                      # optional, default true; false strips them
            },
            "responses": {                 #   POST <base_url>/responses, OpenAI Responses API
              "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_OPENAI_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"}
            }
          },
          "groups": [                      # A/B assignment, percents sum to 100
            {"name": "anthropic-main", "format": "anthropic", "percent": 90},
            {"name": "responses-trial", "format": "responses", "percent": 10}
          ]
        }

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject

`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.

activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

**Why the sweep missed these.** I went back through the session history. The two problems were missed for different reasons, and I was wrong about one of them earlier.

- **The "Sign up" heading over a "Sign in" button wasn't missed.** Three cold readers caught it. It's item 26 of the 40 problems in the report. - **"About 100 messages" really was missed.** That line sits on the first-launch screens. Its reasoning was that a new chat uses Expert while the sign-up credits last. The cold-reader method also can't catch a problem like this one. It sees only screenshots, so it flags unclear sentences. 13:5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
14-6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
15-7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
16:8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.
17-
18:## The cold-reader check
19-
20-The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.
21-
22-- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
23-- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
24-- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
25-- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.
26-
27-What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

Preferences (a modal `PreferencesWindow`, returns on close) and the browser sign-in (loopback callback on port 41172, polled by `CloudSignIn::poll()`) are detours off step 1; when one finishes the controller advances. Nothing a detour does strands the person outside the sequence.
- **Welcome doors:** (superseded for sign-in: it is the in-app form, see [[sign-in-is-the-in-app-form-everywhere]]) Sign in → browser; the card shows "Finish signing in in your browser" with Cancel, other doors dimmed; on the callback the card flips to "Signed in as … · 500 credits", then step 2. Own key / MCP → Preferences › Agent opens modal on that section; saving a verified key or Done closes it and advances; closing unfinished returns to the welcome with nothing chosen. import json,glob,os,re
pat=re.compile(r'(slice for now|skip|generic|default printer|klipper|which printer|printer step|printer screen|printer profile|bottom)',re.I)
seen=set()
files=glob.glob('-Users-kenneth-Projects-claude-cowork-wd/*.jsonl')+glob.glob('-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin*/*.jsonl')
for f in files:
    if os.path.getmtime(f)<1762300000: continue
    for l in open(f,errors='ignore'):
        if '"user"' not in l[:300]: continue
        try: d=json.loads(l)
        except: continue
        if d.get('type')!='user': continue
        ts=d.get('timestamp','')
        if ts<'2026-11-04': continue
        c=d.get('message',{}).get('content')
        if isinstance(c,list):
            c=' '.join(x.get('text','') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('type')=='text')
        if not isinstance(c,str) or len(c)>2500 or c.lstrip().startswith('<') or 'Task (from' in c or 'This session is being continued' in c or 'Background (from' in c: continue
        if 'printer' in c.lower() and pat.search(c):
            k=c[:150]
            if k in seen: continue
            seen.add(k)
            print(ts[:16], os.path.basename(f)[:8], '|', c[:900].replace('\n',' ')); print()
EOF

    c=re.sub(r'\[Image[^\]]*\]','',c).strip()

import json,re,glob,os
pat=re.compile(r'slice for now|default printer|generic printer|bottom of the (list|menu)|which printer|printer profile|skip for now|stand.in printer',re.I)
fs=[f for f in glob.glob('-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin*/*.jsonl') if os.path.getmtime(f)>1762128000]
seen=set()
for f in sorted(fs,key=os.path.getmtime):
    for l in open(f,errors='ignore'):
        try: d=json.loads(l)
        except: continue
        if d.get('type')!='user' or d.get('isSidechain'): continue
        c=d.get('message',{}).get('content')
        if isinstance(c,list): c='\n'.join(x.get('text','') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('type')=='text')
        if not isinstance(c,str): continue
        if 'session is being continued' in c or c.startswith('Task (from') or c.startswith('Base directory') or '<task-notification' in c or 'side-sessions-event' in c: continue
        c=re.sub(r'<([a-z-]+)[^>]*>.*?</\1>','',c,flags=re.S).strip()
        if len(c)>3000 or not pat.search(c): continue
        k=c[:200]
        if k in seen: continue
        seen.add(k)
        print(d.get('timestamp','')[:16],os.path.basename(f)[:8],'|',' '.join(c.split())[:900]); print()
EOF

        c=d.get('message',{}).get('content')
        if isinstance(c,list): c='\n'.join(x.get('text','') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('type')=='text')
        if not isinstance(c,str): continue
        if any(s in c for s in ('session is being continued','cross-session-message','Another Claude session','<task-notification','side-sessions-event','Base directory','[Image')): continue
        c=re.sub(r'<(system-reminder|artifact-view-context)[^>]*>.*?</\1>','',c,flags=re.S)
        c=re.sub(r'\(The JSON line above.*?\)\s','',c,flags=re.S).strip()
        if not c or len(c)>2500: continue
        print(ts[:16],os.path.basename(f)[:8],'|',' '.join(c.split())[:700]);print()
EOF

content.text:
You got the manual "Which printer do you have?" form because of the test command. The design itself works as planned. A new user on your Mac would first see "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?". That screen has the sentence you remember about which printer is set up, and the manual menus come below the list. I found this by reading the code. I haven't launched the app to confirm it.

**Why "Just slice for now" goes to a printer step at all**
- On Nov 2 you said a person must have at least one printer by the end of first launch.
- On Nov 3 you said: "When the user clicks, just slice for now, I want to go back to the onboarding flow."
- On Nov 5 the printer step was designed with three versions. The app picks one:
  - **JusPrin v1 found on the computer:** the step is skipped and a welcome-back window shows.
  - **OrcaSlicer found:** "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" shows. You approved this with "Go with your recommendations."
  - **Neither found:** the manual brand-and-model form shows.

**Why you got the manual form**
- **OrcaSlicer wasn't found.** The app looks for OrcaSlicer's folder beside its own data folder (`OrcaImporter.cpp:122`). With `--datadir /tmp/JusPrin2-stg`, it looked in `/tmp/OrcaSlicer`. That folder doesn't exist, so the app decided you have no OrcaSlicer. Your real OrcaSlicer folder lists six printers with the P1S selected, and the default data folder would have found it.
- **The v1 import never ran.** It only runs when the data folder has no `JusPrin2.conf` yet (`V1Import.cpp:146`). The command writes that file first to point the app at staging, so `JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR` did nothing.

**What I think you remember**
On Nov 6 you approved the review's fixes ("fix all the issues you identified, based on your recommendations"). Two of them changed the OrcaSlicer import screen:
- It gained the line "JusPrin starts with Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle, the printer OrcaSlicer had selected."
- Below the list of printers, "Start fresh" became "Choose my printer instead". That button opens the manual form.

Both are built. I found no message from you saying "the menu is at the bottom of the list", so this is my best guess at what you meant.

**To see that screen on staging**, put the test data folder next to your OrcaSlicer folder:
```bash
D="$HOME/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2-stg"; rm -rf "$D" && mkdir -p "$D" && printf '{"jusprin_server":{"base_url":"https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io"}}\n' > "$D/JusPrin2.conf" && "/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/wording-sweep-fixes/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer" --datadir "$D"
```

worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

(none above = fork-owned)
# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

### First launch against a staging server

First launch looks for OrcaSlicer and JusPrin v1 in their default folders for
the platform (on macOS `~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer` and
`.../JusPrin`), whatever `--datadir` says, and only reads them. Three variables
set up a test run on a throwaway data folder:

- `JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL` names the JusPrin server and wins over
  `jusprin_server.base_url` in the settings file. Use it instead of writing
  the settings file before launch: the v1 import runs only when the data
  folder has no settings file yet.
- `JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR` names another v1 folder; set to `""`, there is none.
- `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` names another OrcaSlicer folder; set to `""`, there
  is none.

Unset, the real folders are used. The shell and real-adapter harnesses point
both folder variables at a folder that does not exist, so they never read a
real install. On Windows an empty variable cannot be set; name a folder that
does not exist instead.

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen

a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then

evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about

concluding anything about the app.

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

First launch: find OrcaSlicer and JusPrin v1 in their real folders, and name the server with a variable

First launch looked for OrcaSlicer and JusPrin v1 in folders beside JusPrin 2's own data folder. A run on a throwaway data folder under /tmp therefore found neither, and a staging test always fell to the manual "Which printer do you have?" form. Writing JusPrin2.conf before launch, the only way to name a staging server, also stopped the v1 import, which runs only when that file does not exist yet.

- Support/AppFolders: one plain-std helper gives an app's default data folder for the platform (macOS ~/Library/Application Support, Windows %APPDATA%, Linux $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config). It is the rule GUI_App applies to its own default data_dir() through wxStandardPaths; the helper is plain std because V1Import and McpCatalog are compiled into the wx-free agent_bridge_tests. McpCatalog's copy of the same rule now uses it.
- OrcaImporter::detect, the File > Import window and V1Import::v1_folder use it, whatever --datadir says. JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR (new) and JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR name another folder; set to "" there is none (Windows cannot hold an empty variable; name a folder that does not exist there).
- JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL wins over jusprin_server.base_url. Every server address (gateway, sign-in, pricing, password reset, print reports) comes from that one function, so a staging run needs no settings file before launch. The v1 import's "no settings file yet" check is unchanged.
- The shell and real-adapter harnesses point both folder variables at a folder that does not exist, so they never read a real install. Before this, a --datadir run skipped v1 by m_datadir_redefined.
- engineering-method.md: how to run first launch against staging.

Upstream file: GUI_App.cpp line 2464 is a fork line (ac55c2961a, not on any upstream branch). It drops the m_datadir_redefined argument, so the fork no longer reads that upstream member. A rebase carries the one-argument call.

Tests: agent_bridge_tests (557 cases, 3 new for the folders and overrides) and jusprin_tests (169) pass. Shell harness default and --fresh-example pass with HOME pointed at a fake v1 and OrcaSlicer folder.
EOF

I committed this as d289298950 on `jusprin-newui-integration`; it isn't pushed. That branch had been deleted in this morning's cleanup, so I recreated it from the tip of `jusprin-newui`. The work is in `.claude/worktrees/real-folder-lookup`.

**What changed**
- **Finding OrcaSlicer and v1.** First launch now looks for both in their usual folders (on a Mac, `~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer` and `.../JusPrin`), whatever `--datadir` says. One shared function holds the per-platform rule. The MCP setup code already had a copy of that rule, and now uses the shared function instead.
- **Override variables.** `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` is new, next to the existing `JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR`. Either one can name a different folder, and setting it to an empty value means "none".
- **Staging address.** The new `JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL` takes priority over the address in the settings file. Every server address in the app comes from one place, so sign-in, AI messages, pricing and print reports all follow it.
- **Harnesses.** The shell harness and the real-adapter harness now point both folder variables at a folder that doesn't exist, so they never read a real install.
- **Docs.** `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` has a short section explaining all this.

**Staging launch commands**

Case (a), v1 import and the welcome-back window:
```bash
D=/tmp/JusPrin2-stg; rm -rf "$D" && JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL=https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/real-folder-lookup/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir "$D"
```

Case (b), a new person who has OrcaSlicer:
```bash
D=/tmp/JusPrin2-stg; rm -rf "$D" && JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL=https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR= /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/real-folder-lookup/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir "$D"
```

**What I tested**
- **Unit tests:** 3 new test cases cover the platform rule and each variable when set, set to empty, and unset. The full agent-bridge suite (557 cases) and the JusPrin suite (169 cases) pass.
- **Shell harness:** I put a fake v1 folder and a fake OrcaSlicer folder in a scratch home folder and ran the default and first-launch modes against it. Both pass, so neither read those folders.
- **Real-adapter harness:** it fails two checks about loading a second model into a project, with or without the scratch home folder. That code path doesn't touch folder lookup, but I didn't run the old build to prove the failures were already there.
- **Case (a), real app:** the v1 import ran from your real v1 folder with no settings file written beforehand. It brought over 2 printers and 4 presets. I deleted that data folder afterwards.

**Still open**

content.text:
The fix is committed as ecaf1d53e0 on jusprin-newui-integration and not pushed. After the JusPrin v1 import, the app now opens the "Welcome back" window first, and the "Profile syncing change" notice about Orca Cloud no longer appears.

**What the problem was.** The v1 import copies v1's settings file into JusPrin 2. That file includes v1's version number, "01.10.01.50". At startup OrcaSlicer treats that number as the version that last saved the settings. Because it is older than 2.4.0, OrcaSlicer opens a notice about profile sync moving from Bambu Cloud to Orca Cloud, and that notice covered the welcome-back window. I confirmed this in the app: before the fix, the window list showed "Profile syncing change".

**The fix.** It is in fork-owned code only, in `carried_settings` in [V1Import.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/V1Import/V1Import.cpp). The import now writes this app's own version (2.4.2), the same value OrcaSlicer writes there at every launch. I first considered erasing the version instead, but OrcaSlicer turns project auto-backup back on when the version is empty. That would undo the setting for anyone who had switched auto-backup off in v1. The other place that reads the old version, the preset updater, doesn't use it, so writing the current version has no other effect. Nothing in GUI_App.cpp changed.

**Tests and results:**
- I added checks to [test_v1_import.cpp](tests/agent/test_v1_import.cpp). The test's v1 settings file now has v1's real version number, and the test checks that JusPrin 2's settings file gets this app's version and keeps the other settings. All 557 test cases in agent_bridge_tests pass.
- In the app, I started from a fresh data folder with the test v1 folder. The imported settings file had version 2.4.2. "Welcome back" opened first, and after 30 seconds the window list still had no "Profile syncing change".
- Screenshot of the welcome-back window: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/0bd9fd0b-1fd6-4ed7-9e9b-89af62d57bfb/scratchpad/after-welcome-back-first.jpg`
- I removed my test data folders and stopped the test app.

**Still open:**
- The screen tool can't click inside the welcome-back page, so I couldn't press Continue to look at the screen after it. The notice is only queued once at startup, though, and it never appeared.
- I didn't run the new test against the old code to watch it fail. The old code copied v1's version unchanged, so the new check would fail there.

content.text:
I removed `JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR` in commit 2ccfeb0a28 on jusprin-newui-integration, not pushed. First launch now always looks for JusPrin v1 in its real folder, whatever `--datadir` says. I made a new commit instead of amending d289298950, because changing that commit would mean rewriting history, and the Orca Cloud fix (ecaf1d53e0) sits on top of it. `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` is unchanged.

The variable had two other jobs, and both still work without it:

- **Keeping the test harnesses away from a real v1 install.** The shell harness and the real-adapter harness write their own settings file before the app starts. The v1 import only runs when there is no settings file, so neither harness ever reads a v1 folder. Their extra setting for the v1 folder is removed; they still point the OrcaSlicer variable at a folder that doesn't exist.
- **Starting as a new person on a Mac that has v1 installed.** Launch with `HOME` pointed at an empty folder, so v1's folder isn't found. Set `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` to the real OrcaSlicer folder so OrcaSlicer is still found. The command is in [engineering-method.md](agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md), in the section "First launch against a staging server".

I also updated v1_folder() and its comment, cut the third test in [test_app_folders.cpp](tests/agent/test_app_folders.cpp) down to one check, and rewrote my saved memory note that described the old setup.

**Tested:**
- All 557 cases in agent_bridge_tests pass.
- The shell harness passes in both its default run and its fresh-install run, with a test v1 install placed in HOME. Neither run showed the welcome-back window.
- I launched the app with an empty HOME on this Mac, which does have v1 installed. No v1 import ran, the app wrote nothing into the fake HOME, and the new-person welcome screen opened. **Not checked:**
- The real-adapter harness was rebuilt but not run. Its edit is the same as the shell harness's, and it already had two failing checks that this work doesn't touch.
- The screen tool can't click inside the welcome page, so I didn't press "Just slice for now" to see the OrcaSlicer import screen in the empty-HOME run.
- The `HOME` recipe is only written and tested for macOS. Windows would need `APPDATA` and Linux `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.
